Touchline · design review · 8 September 2026

The whole pitch.
Every control within reach.

Preserve the dusk control room, club colours, system typography and procedural illustrations. The applied direction repairs alignment, clipping, navigation visibility and input size inside the existing game.

Offline HTML canvas, not a Claude Design document. Artboards are actual browser captures. Pale bands in some screenshots are the recorded SwiftShader rendering limitation, not a proposed surface treatment.

ComparisonsDesign tokensScreen galleryWritten audit

Numeric columns

Each numeric heading shares the right edge of its data column. Original capture uses a different career; compare alignment, not results.

Fixtures

Border-box keeps the complete score inside the card. Passive rows no longer suggest a click. Original capture uses a different career.

Phone tactics

The entire pitch fits. Grid children may shrink; the board retains its 68:92 ratio. Enlarged targets and two-row navigation stay reachable.

Tablet navigation

All seven labels remain visible in the bottom navigation. Its stacking context now sits above page cards.

Settings controls

Small controls now have at least 56px targets, with choices wrapping when necessary.

Club identity

Badge options, palette controls and text fields have larger targets. Input text is 16px. Scroll to reach optional choices.

The game's own system

Values extracted directly from src/ui/styles.ts. Club colours are neutral defaults rebound per career. This sample changes independently of the captured screens.

Type and spacing in use

Body 15px / 1.5; table data 14px; numeric headings 10px; formation title 30px / 800. Card padding 18px; row padding 12px × 16px; grid gap 14px; navigation targets 56px. Radius tokens: 8 / 13 / 20px. These are implementation values, not a new imported scale.
